## Council question

How does the game end on turn ten, especially without Fremen?

## Why this needs a ruling

The live Fremen sheet specifies an end-of-turn-ten special victory, with an ally condition. Recovered JSX resolves games without Fremen using individual points and storm order. The podcast outline mentions sudden death but gives no adopted procedure.

## Answer needed

Confirm whether turn ten remains the last turn, what happens when Fremen is absent, and whether sudden death was actually adopted.

## Provisional drafting approach

Retain the live Fremen condition provisionally; do not invent a sudden-death procedure from the podcast topic.

This is a research question, not an adopted ruling or a claim that Norbert has answered it. No answer has been supplied yet. Keep the affected rules provisional until Norbert or the council confirms them.

## Sources

[Live Fremen](https://dune.zone/factions/fremen); recovered Phases.tsx; podcast planning outline, Sudden Death discussion.

Part of #1831. Record the confirmed answer, its date and a worked example here before closing. Norbert will share this link with the council; this ticket does not send them a message.

comments.body:
Partial ruling, confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026:

> Sudden death is officially adopted, but has never been playtested yet (since very few dreamrules games go to T10)

**Still open:** the sudden-death procedure itself (what triggers it after turn ten, and how a winner is decided), how it relates to the Fremen end-of-turn-ten victory, and what happens when Fremen is not in the game. The rulebook should mark sudden death as adopted but not yet playtested.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

More from Norbert, 14 October 2026:

> Sudden death does not change if fremen is not in the game.
>
> If sudden death ends in no-one being even able to win, then ignore all territories and sectors, all troops count as being in the same territory, and do 1 round of battle, whoever has any remaining troops, wins.
>
> If somehow, not a single player ends that with any forces on the board, the game is officially a draw.

**Recorded:**
- Sudden death works the same whether or not Fremen is in the game.
- **Final battle:** if sudden death ends with no one able to win, ignore all territories and sectors. Every troop on the board counts as being in one territory, and one round of battle is fought. Whoever has any troops left wins.
- **Draw:** if no player has any forces left on the board after that battle, the game is officially a draw.

**Still open:** the sudden-death procedure that runs before this fallback, meaning what happens once turn ten ends and how a winner is found during sudden death. Also how the Fremen end-of-turn-ten victory fits in.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Sudden-death procedure, confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026 (dictated; tidied here):

> After turn 10 is complete after the Nexus phase of turn 10, you keep doing a turn, but skip essentially every single phase and go straight to shipment phase and then battle phase. The Fremen have one special ability during sudden death and that is that they get to do their revival. No other faction is allowed to do revival, so the phases are revival for Fremen, shipment, battle, revival for Fremen, shipment, battle… And of course, after every battle you check if anyone meets the victory conditions and if so, that player or team of players wins.

**Ruling: how the game ends**
1. Turn ten ends after its Nexus phase. If nobody has won, sudden death begins.
2. **Each sudden-death round:** Fremen revival (only Fremen may revive), then shipment and movement, then battle. Every other phase is skipped.
3. **After every battle,** check the normal victory conditions, using the ordered procedure in #1847. A player or alliance that meets them wins.
4. **Final battle:** if sudden death reaches a point where no one can win, ignore territories and sectors. Every troop on the board counts as being in one territory, and one round of battle is fought. Whoever has troops left wins.
5. **Draw:** if no player has forces left on the board after that, the game is a draw.
6. All of this applies the same whether or not Fremen is in the game. Sudden death is adopted but not yet playtested.

**Worked example:** turn ten's Nexus ends with no winner. Sudden-death round one: Fremen revives, everyone ships and moves, and battles are fought. After the Arrakeen battle, Atreides and Emperor hold four strongholds between them, so they win.

**Assumption to confirm:** the Fremen special victory at the end of turn ten (from the live Fremen sheet) is checked before sudden death begins. If that's wrong, reopen this issue.

Closing as answered.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Correction, confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026:

> So there is no special Fremen end of turn 10 victory condition at all. The sudden death is a replacement for any type of default winning conditions, including the Guild and Fremen. It is a replacement.
>
> Now, of course, on turn 10 any faction can normally win the game like on any other turn, but no default.

This replaces the assumption in my previous comment. There is **no** default or special victory at the end of turn ten, for Fremen, Guild or anyone else. During turn ten, any faction can win normally, as on any other turn. If nobody has won when turn ten's Nexus phase ends, sudden death begins. The live Fremen sheet still describes an end-of-turn-ten victory, so it no longer matches this ruling.
